messages:
marta: Heads up — seeing a p95/p99 latency spike in runtime-prod(us-east1) starting ~08:12 UTC. Flamegraphs point to KV cache churn + kernel selector flip to generic path. Trying to correlate with tenant traffic.

kai: on it. which model/route? any noisy tenant id?

marta: route: /v1/generate (model: redwood/gpt-large-8k). noisy tenant looks like tenant_42 — sudden ramp in small requests (len < 50) that broke batching.

lucy: I pulled the profiling traces (attached gist). main hot path is kv_cache::evict -> kv_lookup miss rate jumped to 78% -> batcher fell back to batch_size=1 frequently.

james: that explains kernel mismatch — when batch_size=1 the runtime selects scalar kernels (slow). if we can keep batch>=4 we'll stay on vectorized kernels.

aj: incident-bot created PERF-2026-324 for this: https://redwood.incidents/PERF-2026-324 :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident PERF-2026-324 created by aj. Severity: P2. Runbook: runtime latency surge. Assigned: eng-runtime oncall.

kai: quick mitigation options I can flip now: 1) throttle tenant_42 at router to 50 qps, 2) enable forced batching: min_batch=4 on hot routes, 3) disable prefix_cache_v2 feature flag (it's causing churn). Which do we want?

marta: prefer non-invasive first: throttle tenant_42 to 60 qps and enable min_batch=4 for /v1/generate. will that keep model quality unaffected?

james: yes, batching only affects scheduling. For immediate relief: router throttle + min_batch enforcement. For medium term: we should tune kv cache eviction policy to be LRU with pinning for small prefixes.

lucy: runbook note: how to change min_batch on prod (ops steps):

```
# apply temporary override
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","min_batch":4,"ttl_secs":900}'
```

kai: I applied router throttle (tenant_42 -> 60 qps) at 08:20 UTC. verifying...

infra-bot: Router policy updated for tenant_42: qps_limit=60 by kai at 08:20:37 UTC.

marta: I pushed min_batch=4 override at 08:21. Monitor dashboards.

james: also toggled a kernel hint flag on the hosts to prefer fused_attn_v2 for seq_len<=128 and batch>=4. small risk but should help perf. I rolled it to 10% hosts first.

aj: can we also create a short-term metric to track kv miss rate, batch size distribution, and kernel selection ratio?

lucy: added metrics: runtime.kv.miss_rate, runtime.batcher.batch_size_hist, runtime.kernel.path_ratio. dashboard link: https://grafana/d/abc123/perf-surge

marta: after throttle + min_batch we saw p95 drop from 420ms -> 160ms in 10m window. p99 still elevated (~420ms -> 220ms). good improvement.

kai: next steps (action items):
- kai: keep throttle for 30m, then step down to 80 qps if stable
- james: continue kernel hint canary to 50% hosts if metrics good
- lucy: investigate kv cache config; try eviction_policy=pin-hot-prefixes test in staging
- marta: own post-incident writeup and load repro for perf regression test

marta: assigning owners in incident doc. I'll draft the brief for infra change request (pinning) and link to PERF-2026-324.

james: quick note — if disabling prefix_cache_v2 is needed later, flag name: feature:prefix_cache_v2 (ops toggle). prefer to avoid unless churn continues.

lucy: I ran a synthetic load sim locally replicating tenant_42 pattern. Proposed kv change reduces miss rate from 78% -> 16% in sim. I'll open a PR with config patch and plan to stage it behind a feature flag.

aj: thanks all. leaving this thread open for 1h for rollback/monitoring. If p95/p99 stable for 30m we can de-escalate. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Notice: min_batch override will expire in 15 minutes unless extended (ttl 900s).

marta: extended override TTL to 3600s at 08:37.

kai: will reduce tenant throttle to 80 qps at 08:50 if no regression.

james: if we still see p99 wobble after these mitigations, next step is lightweight kv metric sampling added to runtime to surface hot prefixes. I'll prep the sampling patch.

marta: thanks team. I'll close after 30m stable.

aj: closing note — postmortem template filled, link saved to PERF-2026-324. Follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC.

marta: resolved for now — closing thread after monitoring window. :lock:
